articles.title: Tunable Optical-to-THz Frequency Conversion Driven by Localized Surface Phonon Polaritons in LiNbO3 Metasurfaces
articles.authors: C. McDonnell, M. Ferrera, F. Moia, V. Sajeev, M. Finazzi, A. Toma, C. De Angelis, M. Celebrano, T. Ellenbogen, L. Carletti
institutions: National Institute of Optics − National Research Council (INO−CNR)
articles.summary: We demonstrate tunable THz generation by optical rectification in LiNbO3 rod metasurfaces supporting localized surface phonon polaritons (LSPhPs). By varying the rod length, the LSPhP resonance is tuned across the 4–5 THz range, producing a systematic red-shift of the generated THz spectral peak. THz time-domain spectroscopy and numerical calculations show that the emitted spectrum is governed by the geometry-dependent LSPhP response. …
articles.why: LiNbO3 rod metasurfaces generate THz light by optical rectification, with the output tuned across 4–5 THz simply by changing rod length to shift a localized surface phonon polariton resonance. THz time-domain spectroscopy and calculations show the emitted spectrum is set by this geometry-dependent phonon-polariton response, giving a design handle for THz sources.

articles.title: SERS-Active Nanocomposite Contact Lenses for Label-Free Multiplexed Biosensing of Tear Analytes
articles.authors: Ahmed E. Salih, Connie M. Wang, Roberta M. Sabino, Loza F. Tadesse, Elazer R. Edelman
articles.summary: Continuous monitoring remains limited by the fact that most wearable biosensors are built around single-analyte recognition chemistries, even though many physiological states are defined by changes across multiple metabolites. Tear fluid is one of the most biochemically informative biofluids accessible non-invasively, but contact lens biosensors have largely relied on enzymatic or electrochemical techniques that are difficult to extend beyond one target marker at a time. Here, we report a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-active contact lens in which gold nanostars are grown in situ on commercial hydrogel contact lenses. …
articles.why: Gold nanostars grown in situ on commercial hydrogel contact lenses make them SERS-active for label-free, multiplexed sensing of tear analytes. This moves wearable tear sensing beyond the one-analyte-at-a-time limit of enzymatic and electrochemical lenses.

articles.title: Operando Imaging of Battery Interfaces through Combined Analysis of Broadband Optical Backgrounds and Raman Features
articles.authors: Shengfu Wei, Zhengcheng Gu, Yufeng Zhang, Weigang Ma, Aoran Fan, Xing Zhang
articles.summary: Solid-state batteries promise improved safety and energy density, but their performance is governed by buried interfaces where ion transport, chemical reactions, and stress evolution are strongly coupled. Resolving these processes during operation remains challenging. Here, we present an operando spectroscopic strategy that jointly analyzes broadband optical backgrounds and characteristic electrolyte Raman features within a single measurement. …
articles.why: Rather than discarding the broadband optical background, this operando method analyses it jointly with electrolyte Raman bands in a single measurement to image buried solid-state battery interfaces during operation. It turns a usual nuisance signal into extra information about coupled interfacial processes.

articles.title: Droplet-Shielded Micropore Raman-Activated Cell Sorting Improves Recovery of Emerging-Contaminant-Degrading Microorganisms
articles.authors: Jibing Li, Xixi Cai, Ying Xue, Jiarui Liu, Weiping Mei, Qiqian Li, Longfei Jiang, Dayi Zhang, Bei Li, Chunling Luo
institutions: Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Joint Laboratory for Environmental Pollution and Control
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
articles.summary: Identifying, isolating, and cultivating functional microorganisms from complex environmental microbiomes remains a central challenge in linking microbial identity with contaminant transformation. Conventional Raman-activated cell sorting (RACS) enables label-free single-cell phenotyping but often compromises cell viability during laser interrogation and ejection, limiting the cultivation of functional indigenous microorganisms. Tire-wear-derived 6PPD-quinone (6PPDQ) is increasingly recognized as a highly toxic emerging contaminant in roadside soils, yet the indigenous microorganisms associated with its biological attenuation in roadside soils remain poorly characterized. …
articles.why: A droplet-shielded micropore design for Raman-activated cell sorting protects cells during laser interrogation and ejection, addressing the poor viability that limits conventional RACS. It is used to recover and cultivate soil microbes linked to degradation of the tire-wear toxicant 6PPD-quinone.

articles.title: Chip-scale differential near-infrared spectroscopy in strongly water-absorbing environments
articles.authors: Chunhui Yao, Tongyun Li, Richard Penty
articles.summary: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy enables nondestructive chemical analysis, yet quantitative measurements in aqueous environments are fundamentally hindered by water’s dominant, broadband absorption. This strong background obscures weak analyte signatures and can destabilize spectral inference in chip-scale spectrometers. Here, we demonstrate a chip-scale differential NIR spectrometer based on an integrated bidirectional photonic circuit that operates robustly in strongly water-absorbing environments. …
articles.why: A chip-scale differential NIR spectrometer built on an integrated bidirectional photonic circuit cancels the overwhelming broadband water background that normally swamps weak analyte bands. This makes quantitative on-chip NIR measurements robust in strongly water-absorbing samples.

articles.title: Modified lithium-ion cell design enabling operando gas sensing using optical fiber photothermal spectroscopy
articles.authors: Zongchang Luo, Fangyuan Han, Longfei Zhang, Qinqin Liang, Bin Tang, Jiqi Pan, Min Yu
institutions: Guangxi Key Laboratory of Intelligent Control and Maintenance of Power Equipment
articles.summary: A modified lithium-ion cell integrated with a hollow-core fiber photothermal spectroscopy (HCF-PTS) sensor was developed for operando monitoring of gas evolution during electrochemical cycling. The platform enabled simultaneous measurements of cell voltage, internal pressure, and gas-phase concentrations of C 2 H 4 and CO 2 in a sealed LiFePO 4 /graphite cell. The HCF-PTS system with limits of detection of 1.2 ppm for C 2 H 4 and 1.7 ppm for CO 2 were obtained. Measurements from two independently assembled modified cells showed similar voltage, pressure, and gas-evolution profiles, demonstrating good reproducibility under the present experimental conditions. …
articles.why: A hollow-core-fibre photothermal spectroscopy sensor built into a modified lithium-ion cell tracks C2H4 and CO2 evolution at ppm level operando, alongside voltage and internal pressure. It brings laser gas spectroscopy inside a working sealed battery.

articles.title: Light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy based on Quartz-PZT dual-resonance enhancement method for high-sensitivity gas sensing
articles.authors: Ma Hanxu, Song Yushuo, Cai Jingze, Qiao Shunda, He Ying, Sun Haiyue, Sampaolo Angelo, Spagnolo Vincenzo, Ma Yufei
articles.why: Introduces a quartz–PZT dual-resonance enhancement scheme for light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES), aimed at boosting gas-sensing sensitivity beyond a single quartz tuning-fork detector.

articles.title: High‐Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging
articles.authors: Zhanqiang Xue, Hongyang Xing, Guizhen Xu, Junxing Fan, Zijian Liao, Ye Zhou, Longqing Cong
articles.summary: Metasurface‐enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high‐throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade‐off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction‐enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high‐quality‐factor resonances. …
articles.why: Pixelated metasurfaces built from photonic-crystal heterojunctions encode spatial position directly into distinct high-Q terahertz resonances, enabling hyperspectral THz imaging without discrete spectral sampling or computational reconstruction. It sidesteps the usual trade-off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal metasurfaces.

articles.title: Raman‐Enabled Platicon Microcomb and Stokes Soliton in 4H‐SiC Microresonator
articles.authors: Jingwei Li, Ruixuan Wang, Qing Li
articles.summary: Stimulated Raman scattering in Kerr microresonators is generally regarded as a competing nonlinear process that hinders the formation of Kerr soliton microcombs. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that the ubiquitous Raman gain in Kerr microresonators can instead be harnessed to enable efficient platicon microcomb generation in the normal‐dispersion regime. We demonstrate this mechanism in a compact silicon carbide microresonator supporting a broadband platicon microcomb spanning 1500–1700 nm with a pump‐to‐comb conversion efficiency as high as . …
articles.why: Instead of treating stimulated Raman scattering as a nuisance for Kerr microcombs, this work harnesses Raman gain in a 4H-SiC microresonator to generate platicon microcombs in the normal-dispersion regime, together with a Stokes soliton. It turns an unavoidable vibrational nonlinearity into a comb-generation tool.

articles.title: Non‐Pixelated Spatial‐Spectral Imaging via Electrically Tunable Lateral Photocarrier Dynamics in a MoS 2 /p‐Ge Position‐Sensitive Detector
articles.authors: Kaiyang Liu, Di Wang, Wentao Liu, Peiyu Zeng, Dingli Guo, Wenhui Wang, Zhenhua Ni, Junpeng Lu
articles.summary: Spectral sensitivity is essential for advanced visual perception, including object identification, material discrimination, and high‐fidelity color reproduction. However, conventional spectral imaging systems often rely on pixel‐level wavelength‐selective filters, sacrificing spatial resolution and limiting spectral discrimination, or on vertically stacked heterostructures with electrically tunable band alignment, which increase fabrication complexity and array nonuniformity. …
articles.why: A MoS2/p-Ge position-sensitive detector uses electrically tunable lateral photocarrier dynamics to obtain spatial and spectral information without pixelated filters or stacked heterostructures. This offers a simpler route to spectral imaging that does not sacrifice spatial resolution.

articles.title: Photonic Integrated Circuits for End‐to‐End Spectral Analysis: Computational Sampling With Neural Network Reconstruction
articles.authors: Yuhang Wang, Ang Li, Xiaozhuo Zhao, Yang Zhao, Qiang Li, Ye Tian, Shilong Pan
articles.summary: On‐chip spectral analysis enables transformative applications, from smartphone‐based glucose monitoring to UAV‐mounted remote sensing. While progress has been made in on‐chip spectral sampling, on‐chip spectral reconstruction remains a critical unmet need as current approaches rely upon computer to run complex algorithms. Here, we report an on‐chip solution for end‐to‐end spectral analysis by combining high‐resolution spectral sampling and real‐time high‐fidelity spectral reconstruction on CMOS compatible platform. …
articles.why: Combines high-resolution computational spectral sampling and real-time neural-network spectral reconstruction on one CMOS-compatible photonic chip, removing the need for an external computer to recover spectra. A step toward fully self-contained miniature spectrometers.

articles.title: Nonlinear Phonon-Assisted Up-Conversion Photoluminescence Under Vibrational Pumping at Liquid-Helium Temperatures
articles.authors: Chang H, Lai JM, Song F, Lv Y, Zhang J
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
School of Materials Science and Engineering of Shanxi Normal University
articles.summary: Optical refrigeration in semiconductors is driven by anti-Stokes photoluminescence (PL) arising from phonon-assisted up-conversion. In the conventional picture, lattice vibrations remain in thermal equilibrium and the relevant phonon population is pump independent, so the up-conversion rate scales approximately linearly with excitation power, which places a practical limit on cooling power density and predicts a rapid collapse of cooling efficiency at cryogenic temperatures. …
articles.why: Shows that phonon-assisted up-conversion photoluminescence becomes nonlinear under vibrational pumping at liquid-helium temperatures, contrary to the conventional picture of a pump-independent thermal phonon population. This bears directly on the limits of optical refrigeration of semiconductors at cryogenic temperatures.

articles.title: FRACTAL: A Ratiometric-based Fingerprinting Framework for Robust Spectral Classification and Ratio-based Spectroscopic Marker Discovery
articles.authors: Lamyaa M. Almehmadi
articles.summary: Spectral classification is conventionally performed on band intensities, yet ratios between bands have long served as diagnostic indices in vibrational spectroscopy, from lipid-to-protein markers of membrane composition to amide ratios reporting protein secondary structure. Their use, however, has remained confined to a handful of expert-selected pairs, leaving most of the ratio information contained in a spectrum unexamined. Here I present FRACTAL (Full Ratio Combinatorial Analysis for Classification and Analytical Interpretation), which computes every pairwise log-intensity ratio among detected peaks to form a complete ratiometric fingerprint, grounded in compositional data analysis. …
articles.why: FRACTAL computes every pairwise log-intensity ratio among detected peaks to build a complete ratiometric fingerprint, grounded in compositional data analysis. It extends band-ratio analysis beyond the handful of expert-selected pairs used until now, so more of the ratio information in a spectrum can be used for classification and marker discovery.

Without miR-10b, Cy5 is fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-quenched by AuNPs (low FL) but SERS-enhanced by localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) (strong SERS). …

Based on quantitative analysis of gaseous products, two distinct discharge modes (O3 mode and NOx mode) of surface dielectric barrier discharge plasma were identified. …

Methods We analysed NIRS readings of six computed tomography angiography (CTA)‐confirmed LVO‐stroke patients at Tampere University Hospital during the six‐month study period. We placed four sensors on patients’ heads: two frontally and two parietally. We provided a detailed description and analysis of these recordings and their correlation with imaging‐confirmed changes in perfusion. …

articles.summary: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy was applied to investigate the adsorption behavior of ethylene on ZSM-5 zeolites containing Na+, Ag+, and H+ sites. Ethylene adsorbed on Na+ and Ag+ sites could be distinguished by its characteristic NIR absorption band. Further, ethylene adsorbed on Brønsted acid sites was identified by the formation of protonated ethyl species. Temperature-dependent measurements also revealed distinct desorption behaviors associated with different cation sites. The applicability of NIR spectroscopy was further demonstrated by in situ monitoring of ethanol dehydration over Ag+0.5/H+0.5/ZSM-5. Upon ethanol adsorption, ethoxy species were first formed on Brønsted acid sites. …

Conventional wide-FoV optics rely on bulky compound refractive optics, limiting miniaturization. Metalenses composed of sub-wavelength meta-atoms offer a compact alternative. However, achieving high transmission and complete 2 π phase coverage simultaneously over wide angle-of-incidence (AOI) remains challenging, leading to blur and non-uniform efficiency across the field. Here, we present a learned π metalens based on an AOI-aware design framework that achieves uniform-quality 100° FoV NIR imaging. …

Here we focus on the evaluation of the performances of the infrared channel of the Moons and Jupiter Imaging Spectrometer (MAJIS) based on Earth observations acquired over part of the Pacific Ocean at tropical latitudes. We specifically compare MAJIS observations with nearly co-located ones from the Infrared Atmospheric Sounding Interferometer (IASI). The two instruments overlap in the spectral range 3.6 and 5.56 µm. …

Some studies used Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to analyze hematite and goethite. The objective of this study was to identify absorption bands in FTIR of synthetic (oxyhydr)-oxides that allow to distinguish hematite, goethite, and ferrihydrite and to compare the FTIR of iron (oxyhydr)-oxides synthesized in the laboratory with soil born ones. …

articles.summary: To remain safe and actionable, multi-component gas-phase Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) process analysis requires a reliability estimate for each concentration prediction. In a semi-synthetic feasibility study for a fixed compound library, we present a Bayesian one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) trained on spectra from single-compound reference data that predicts concentrations, compound presence probabilities and per-prediction uncertainty bounds. The model yields accurate concentration predictions (mean absolute error 0.165 in log 10 -space, within a factor of about 1.5) and uncertainty bounds that remain well-calibrated under severe instrumental artifacts. …
